messages.subject: Scaled histogram? Position of strip.text()?
parts:
Dear all,

I am polishing up graphs for a submission. Two things keep irking
people who look at them. Here's an example:

name <- rep(c("Panel A","Panel B","Panel C","Panel D"), 250)
value <- c(rnorm(500), rgamma(500, 1,1))
type <- c(rep("Alpha", 500), rep("Beta", 500))
out <- data.frame(Name=name, Value=value, Type=type)

g <- ggplot(data=out, aes(x=Value, y=..scaled..)) +
geom_density(size=1.4) + facet_grid(Name ~ Type, scales="free")
g <- g + opts(panel.background=theme_blank(),
axis.line=theme_segment(), strip.text.y = theme_text())
g <- g + scale_y_continuous(breaks=0, labels="") + labs(x="", y="")
g <- g + geom_line(data=data.frame(Type="Alpha", x=c(0,0),
y=c(0,1.1)), aes(x=x, y=y), size=1, colour="black")
g <- g + geom_line(data=data.frame(Type="Beta", x=c(1.65,1.65),
y=c(0,1.1)), aes(x=x, y=y), size=1, colour="black")
print(g)

1) If I change geom_density() to geom_histogram(), the y=..scaled.. no
longer works. How would I get a scaled histogram for each of the
grids?
2) Hadley wrote in July that by the end of summer, an option might
become available that I can move the strip.text() to the left side of
the graph. Has that been implemented yet? What would be the option/
command?

Thanks so much.
Best
Toby

messages.subject: Re: Scaled histogram? Position of strip.text()?
parts:
Hi:

Notice that stat_bin() does not have 'scaled' as an option:
 
     stat_density():   density, count, scaled
     stat_bin():  count, density, ncount, ndensity

However, ..scaled.. in stat_density() is analogous to ..ndensity.. in stat_bin(). (Check their respective online help pages at
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/  for more details.) So one way to compare scaled kernel density estimates and scaled histograms (max = 1)

g + geom_density(aes(y = ..scaled..), size = 1) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..ndensity..)) +

But...the two don't necessarily agree visually. This makes sense since the two summaries are independently maximized at 1. So try

g + geom_density(aes(y = ..density..), size = 1, fill = 'orange', alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), fill = 'blue') +

which looks more compatible to me. Coloring the histogram and providing a fill color for the density plots (with alpha transparency) adds some visual sugar and provides some differentiation between the density plot and the histogram.

This may not be exactly what you want, but it does show a couple of ways to plot the histogram (including scaling to a max of 1) and how to superimpose the histogram and density plot, if that is of interest at all. You can fine tune the details to get what you want.

Does that help?
Dennis
